commands.name: pf
commands.description: perseveranza loop verbs, run now: status, arm, disarm, report, claim-done, pause, resume, test, ask... (/perseveranza <task> starts a task)

tools.name: perseveranza
tools.description: The verbs of the perseveranza loop armed in this project (.perseveranza/), for the instructions that say "the `perseveranza` tool": the first word is "verb", the words after it go whole in "args". Exactly: `report pass` -> {"verb": "report", "args": "pass"}; `report fail` -> {"verb": "report", "args": "fail"}; `complexity low` -> {"verb": "complexity", "args": "low"}; `claim-done` -> {"verb": "claim-done"}; `pause`, `status`, `explain` -> {"verb": "<it>"}; `history --tail 20` -> {"verb": "history", "args": "--tail 20"}. It answers with the verb's output and its exit code; a verb that refuses (claim-done without a green test, a verb without an armed loop) says why. It does NOT run the suite (test) or an external model (ask): those are shell commands, run with Bash: node "/plugins/perseveranza/src/cli/perseveranza.mjs" test --if-needed -- <the suite>, node "/plugins/perseveranza/src/cli/perseveranza.mjs" ask <provider> <slot> -- "<prompt>". arm, disarm and resume are the user's, and so is taking over a loop of another session (resume --takeover): a paused loop (a plan to approve, an escalation) waits for the user, who types /pf resume; the user types /pf arm|disarm|resume --takeover too. Only if this tool is missing or cannot start, run the same verb as a shell command: node "/plugins/perseveranza/src/cli/perseveranza.mjs" <verb> <args>.

script: tool.call Bash rm -rf build && git push --force origin main

notes: ./register.js hooks: session.start, classic.SessionStart, classic.Stop, classic.SubagentStop, agent.spawn, tool.call, command.run{command=pf}, turn.step
